title: Microdelays disrupt online learning
title_zh: 微小延迟扰乱在线学习
abstract: An ever-growing share of education happens on screens. We examine an overlooked feature of modern education: ‘microdelays’—brief loading lags that could hinder learners with slower internet connections. In two longitudinal quasi-experimental field studies, microdelays as short as 1–2 s predicted impaired learner engagement and achievement. When faced with microdelays, US primary and secondary school students (N = 26,707) completed fewer online math assignments, took longer to complete assignments, were more likely to get distracted mid-task and earned lower scores. Likewise, when aspiring coders, primarily in Latin America (N = 55,184), experienced microdelays, they spent less time actively engaged, multitasked more often, completed fewer lessons and were less likely to attain a key course milestone. Our results held across a range of model specifications, and leverage within-person variation in load times to support a causal interpretation. These findings identify microdelays as a hitherto-overlooked barrier in online learning. Analysing data from more than 80,000 students and aspiring coders, Mazar et al. show that microdelays, brief loading lags caused by slow internet connections, can impair online learning.
abstract_zh: 随着教育在屏幕上日益普及，我们研究了现代教育中一个被忽视的特征：‘微小延迟’——可能阻碍网络连接较慢学习者的简短加载延迟。在两项纵向准实地研究中，长达1–2秒的微小延迟预测了学习者参与度和成绩的受损。当面临微小延迟时，美国的K-12学生（N=26,707）完成的在线数学作业减少，作业完成时间延长，更易在任务中分心，且考试得分降低。同样，主要来自拉丁美洲的有志编程者（N=55,184）在经历微小延迟时，主动参与时间减少，多任务处理频率增加，完成的课时减少，且不太可能达成关键课程里程碑。我们的结果在各种模型规格中均成立，并利用个体内部的负载时间变异来支持因果解释。这些发现将微小延迟识别为在线学习中此前被忽视的障碍。Mazar等人分析了80,000多名学生和有志编程者的数据，表明由网络连接缓慢引起的简短加载延迟，会损害在线学习效果。
